metadata.title: This Week: Done, and Where I Helped
metadata.register: Professional, polite, simple -- a real progress update, not overhyped, per the user's explicit tone request.
metadata.note: A CLI-explainer weekly recap -- a NEW week's log, separate from the earlier weekly-recap builds (weekly-recap, -catbot, -suffolk, -never-forgets, -tutor, -mcphs, -hotel). Same story spine as those builds (B00 cold open -> problem -> ask -> code -> output -> change -> code -> output -> lesson -> handoff -> outro; real code shown via ClaudeCodeBeat; one required revision cycle). weekly_recap_v1.py and weekly_recap_v2.py are genuine Python scripts, both actually run; v1 is a flat list of four entries, v2 adds the user's ROLE to each (author / attendee / support / producer) and prints a done-vs-supporting count -- chosen because the user asked for an honest update that says they HELPED Yatra with the social media strategy rather than led it. THE STRATEGY IS NOT DESCRIBED beyond 'I helped with it' (user instruction): the social-media graphic is a phone with abstract, generic post icons (a heart outline, a speech bubble, a share arrow, blank image tiles) and NO real platform logos. HOMES OF HOPE VISUALS ARE ABSTRACT (user instruction): a calendar and a film-clapper outline only -- no photos, no people shapes. Video count: the user's kickoff says 'four videos'; this session produced the ai-colleague-quota video and this recap, each in two formats (two videos, four files in total). Consistent with the user's own earlier note on the previous recap ('two videos, each exported in 16:9 and 9:16, four files in total, so the narration is accurate'), that accurate wording is used and flagged at delivery. Disclosed substitutions carried forward: (1) af_bella + @HumanitariansAI instead of the skill's default voice/handle; (2) rendered through run.sh/compile.py/static_scene_check.py/manim_layout_audit.py/final_frame_check.py. Self-intro ('Hi, I'm Agrima') folds into B00's own narration per the cli-explainer skill's convention. All items are the user's own self-reported account. No footage exists -- every visual is a generated Manim graphic.

beats.role_note: the real weekly_recap_v1.py output, visualized as four same-weight cards (the three parts: writing, Homes of Hope documentary, video production)
beats.narration_text: Run it, and here's the week. One article on Substack, The AI Colleague With a Quota, about how sales teams are adding AI agents that handle the research and the first hello, so people can spend more time on the conversations that matter. Meetings for the Homes of Hope documentary, a project that supports marginalized girls in India with a safe home, education, and support. Help for Yatra with the social media strategy for the documentary, so the girls' stories can reach a wider audience. And two videos on Brutalist, each taken through planning, review, approvals, and export, in sixteen by nine and nine by sixteen: four files in total.
beats.visual_intent: four same-weight cards: mock Substack header ('The AI Colleague With a Quota'); a meeting/calendar card for the Homes of Hope documentary; a phone with abstract post icons labeled 'Social media strategy for the documentary (with Yatra)'; two videos each split into 16:9 + 9:16, all checked

beats.role_note: the revision ask -- add a role to each item and count
beats.narration_text: But a flat list hides my role in each. So: add a role to every item, and count them.
